entries.title: After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces

entries.snippet: The Republican president will now visit Iowa and Kansas for back-to-back campaign rallies on Sunday. Both events had previously been canceled for a slew of telerallies.

entries.title: Massive Gen Z protests set to sweep cities across Germany
entries.snippet: Young people in Germany are taking to the streets in some 34 cities, calling for greater political say and a more hopeful future. The protests come amid a wave of youth demonstrations across Europe. DW has more.

entries.title: Bollywood and the underworld — together in the spotlight?
entries.snippet: A wave of shootings and extortion threats has rattled India's film industry. This time, those claiming responsibility are very different from the Mumbai underworld that had Bollywood in its grip back in the 1990s.

entries.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
entries.snippet: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

entries.title: India news: Amit Shah challenges Rahul Gandhi to debate vote theft in Parliament
entries.snippet: Home Minister Amit Shah has challenged Rahul Gandhi to debate electoral irregularity allegations in parliament, ahead of a major opposition rally against the election chief in Delhi. DW has more.

entries.title: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara to expire amid US, Russia vetoes
entries.snippet: The mandate of the UN peacekeeping force in Western Sahara will expire on October 31. The UN Security Council could not agree on a resolution to extend the mission.

entries.title: European diplomats shun Russia at G20 gathering in the US
entries.snippet: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov declined to comment on Russia's participation in the G20 summit in December, telling DW that Volodymyr Zelenskyy should travel to Russia if he wanted talks with Vladimir Putin.

entries.title: Poland: Protesters clash with police over sacked court chief
entries.snippet: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk defended the firing of top court President Bogdan Swieczkowski as a move to "restore the rule of law."

entries.title: Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

entries.title: Ukraine: Oleshky residents evacuate war-ravaged city
entries.snippet: Under the local ceasefire, an aid convoy of 25 buses arrived with humanitarian aid and as transport for fleeing Oleshky residents. The Ukrainian city has been occupied by Russia since 2022 and faces food shortages.

entries.title: Smuggling, power, profit: Irregular migration out of eastern Libya
entries.snippet: There is currently more irregular migration between eastern Libya and Crete, Greece. It's raising questions as to what connects people smugglers with powerful militias in eastern Libya and then in turn, Europeans.

entries.title: Tennessee woman Christa Pike describes pain after failed execution
entries.snippet: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain a month after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee. Her lawyers want her death sentence reduced to life, while the state governor has ordered an investigation.

entries.title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
entries.snippet: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?

entries.title: US midterms: Pope Leo XIV casts vote by mail
entries.snippet: As a US citizen, Pope Leo XIV is eligible to vote in US elections and has made use of that right with a postal ballot ahead of Tuesday's midterms. The pontiff, a Chicago native, did not reveal who he voted for.

entries.title: Binance crypto exchange suspends trades over North Korea-linked hack
entries.snippet: Crypto platform Binance has suspended trading following a suspected hack now linked to North Korea. The disruption has left users unable to trade on the cryptocurrency platform while the suspected breach is investigated.

entries.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
entries.snippet: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.

entries.title: Seoul fears being sidelined as US reaches out to North Korea
entries.snippet: With ties between South Korea and the Trump administration strained, the South Korean government worries that Donald Trump's pursuit of a diplomatic breakthrough with Kim Jong Un may come at Seoul's expense.

entries.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
entries.snippet: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

entries.title: Italy: Students and workers rally over living costs
entries.snippet: Students and workers have marched across Italy for more school funding and relief from rising living costs. The rallies follow weeks of school occupations and protests against higher military spending.

entries.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
entries.snippet: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.
